question_text: In an A/B test, what are "subjects"?

possible_answers.C: The outcome variables measured in a study
possible_answers.D: The software used to analyze data

explanation: In experimental design, 'subjects' refer to the individual units (such as users, patients, or web sessions) that are randomly assigned to be exposed to the different experimental treatments.

question_text: In a properly designed A/B test, which of the following methods is used to assign subjects to the control and treatment groups?
explanation: Randomization ensures that each subject has an equal chance of being assigned to either group, minimizing selection bias and ensuring the groups are comparable.

question_text: The main purpose of the control group in an A/B test is to:
explanation: The control group represents the status quo (the existing version). It provides a baseline metric so researchers can accurately measure if the new treatment actually caused a significant change.

possible_answers.A: A statement that the treatment always produces an effect
possible_answers.B: A claim that any observed difference is due to chance
possible_answers.C: The preferred outcome that the researcher expects to confirm
possible_answers.D: A hypothesis that eliminates measurement error

explanation: The null hypothesis always takes the position of skepticism: it assumes there is no real effect or relationship, and any difference observed in the sample data is simply random statistical noise.

question_text: The alternative hypothesis is best described as:

possible_answers.A: The assumption that no relationship exists between variables
possible_answers.B: The explanation that supports random sampling error
possible_answers.C: The competing claim that suggests a real effect or difference exists
possible_answers.D: A hypothesis used only when results are statistically insignificant

explanation: The alternative hypothesis is the theory that the researcher is usually trying to prove; it claims that the treatment did have a statistically significant effect or that a real relationship exists.

possible_answers.B: The extent of association between two paired variables
possible_answers.C: The probability that two variables are independent
possible_answers.D: The variability within a single datasets

explanation: The correlation coefficient (ranging from -1 to 1) quantifies the strength and direction of the linear relationship or association between two paired numerical variables.

question_text: In a permutation test, resamples are created by:

possible_answers.A: Generating new synthetic observations from a statistical model
possible_answers.B: Drawing samples independently from each group with replacement
possible_answers.C: Randomly reallocating existing observations among groups

explanation: A permutation test combines all the data from the groups, shuffles the labels, and randomly redistributes the exact same observations back into groups to see how likely the original difference was.

question_text: A blind study is best defined as a study in which:

possible_answers.A: Investigators do not collect outcome data directly
possible_answers.B: Subjects are unaware of which treatment they are receiving
possible_answers.C: Treatments are randomly assigned to participants
possible_answers.D: Researchers conceal the study hypothesis from participants

explanation: In a blind (or single-blind) study, the participants do not know whether they are receiving the experimental treatment or the placebo, which prevents the placebo effect from skewing the results.

question_text: Why are A/B tests commonly used in marketing and e-commerce?

possible_answers.B: They allow comparison between two treatments
possible_answers.D: They remove the need for statistical analysis

explanation: A/B tests allow marketers to show two variations (A and B) to users simultaneously and use data to directly compare which treatment drives better performance metrics.

question_text: In which study design are neither the participants nor the investigators aware of treatment assignments?
explanation: A double-blind study conceals the group assignment from both the subjects (preventing placebo effects) and the researchers interacting with them (preventing observer bias).

question_text: Which of the following statements correctly describes a null hypothesis (H₀) in hypothesis testing?

possible_answers.A: It claims that there is a significant effect or difference in the population.
possible_answers.B: It states that any observed difference is due to the treatment being tested.
possible_answers.C: It assumes no effect, no difference, or no relationship exists in the population.
possible_answers.D: It predicts the direction of change, such as an increase or decrease.

explanation: The core definition of H₀ is the assumption of the 'status quo'—that nothing interesting is happening and there is no underlying difference or effect in the population.

question_text: Information about samples is observed, and information about large populations is often .................... from smaller samples.
explanation: Statistical inference is the act of using data drawn from a smaller sample to make generalized estimates or predictions (inferences) about the broader population.

question_text: A histogram graph with its tail extending towards the right side is referred to as being
explanation: When the tail stretches into the higher (positive) values on the right side of the x-axis, the data is described as right-skewed or positively skewed.

question_text: A histogram graph with most of the data points being to the left side is called
explanation: If the bulk of the data is clustered on the left side, it forces the tail to stretch out to the right side. Therefore, it is right-skewed, which is synonymous with positively skewed.

question_text: For events that occur at a constant rate, the number of events per unit of time or space can be modeled as:
explanation: The Poisson distribution is specifically formulated to express the probability of a given number of independent events occurring in a fixed interval of time or space, given a constant mean rate.

question_text: The two main types of resampling procedure are _______.

possible_answers.D: Sampling with replacement and stratified sampling

explanation: Bootstrapping (which draws samples with replacement to estimate confidence intervals) and permutation tests (which shuffle labels for hypothesis testing) are the two fundamental resampling methods.
